Health Domain - Compliance and Legal Requirements

HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR 164.508) requires explicit patient consent for certain uses and disclosures of PHI.

For Patient Consent Management: Required attributes include patient identifier, consent type (treatment, disclosure, research), consent date, consent form signature (electronic or physical), witness information if required, expiration date if applicable, and revocation capability. Purpose of consent must be clearly stated. Patient capacity to consent must be verified.

For Medical Audit: Required attributes include audit scope (patient population, date range, service type), access logs (who accessed what PHI when), modification logs, and audit trail integrity verification. Patient identifiers may be anonymized for statistical audits. Specific patient identifiers required only for targeted audits.

For Clinical Trial Management: Required attributes include participant identifier, informed consent documentation, inclusion/exclusion criteria verification, randomization assignment (if blinded trial), adverse event reports, and data collection forms per protocol. IRB approval documentation required. Sponsor and principal investigator information.

For Regulatory Reporting: Required attributes include report type (adverse events, quality metrics, public health reporting), required data elements per regulation, reporting entity identification, and submission dates. Patient identifiers may be de-identified for aggregate reporting. Specific identifiers required for adverse event reporting to FDA.

For Accreditation Management: Required attributes include facility identifier, accreditation standard compliance documentation, quality metrics, patient safety indicators, and survey dates. Patient-level data may be aggregated for accreditation reporting. Specific patient identifiers not required unless for case reviews.

UNNECESSARY Attributes: Religion, ethnicity, political affiliation are unnecessary for compliance purposes unless required by specific reporting regulations. Social media information is not required.

HIPAA Breach Notification Rule (45 CFR 164.400-414) requires notification if unsecured PHI is accessed, acquired, used, or disclosed in violation of Privacy Rule.

GDPR Article 6(1)(c) - Legal Obligation: Processing is lawful when necessary for compliance with legal obligation.
